appealpilot.llmDetail: Yes. src/lib/clients/ai-provider.ts (generateWithAI) POSTs to `${NEBIUS_BASE_URL}/chat/completions` with Bearer NEBIUS_API_KEY, body {model: NEBIUS_MODEL, messages, max_tokens:2000, temperature:0.7} — a standard OpenAI-compatible chat call against Nebius. It is invoked from src/lib/appeal/generator.ts (generateAppealPackage) to produce the appeal letter/email/phone-script JSON, and orchestrated in src/app/api/appeal/build/route.ts. Provider is Nebius only (no OpenAI/Anthropic SDK present); model is fully env-configured. If keys are unset it falls back to hardcoded templates (buildFromTemplates).
appealpilot.gpuDetail: No GPU need. package.json dependencies are only next ^15.3.9, react ^19, react-dom ^19, lucide-react — a pure Next.js/TypeScript frontend with serverless API routes. No torch/cuda/tensorflow/transformers/onnx, no embeddings, no training/fine-tuning, no self-hosted model serving. Denial-letter parsing is regex-based (src/lib/appeal/parser.ts); Tavily (web search) and mem0 (memory) are remote HTTP APIs. All inference is delegated to a hosted LLM endpoint.
appealpilot.evidence: src/lib/clients/ai-provider.ts already calls a Nebius OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint (NEBIUS_BASE_URL/NEBIUS_MODEL/NEBIUS_API_KEY) for appeal-package generation in generator.ts, and README/route.ts list Nebius as the inference provider — a perfect serverless-inference (Token Factory) fit, swappable to any open model (Llama/Qwen/DeepSeek/gpt-oss) by changing only env vars. Dependency manifest (package.json: next/react/react-dom/lucide-react only) shows no torch/cuda/embeddings/training, so there is essentially no AI Cloud GPU-cluster need.

armo.llmDetail: No LLM usage anywhere. package.json dependencies are purely client-side: phaser ^4.1.0, three ^0.184.0, react ^19, zustand ^5 — no openai/anthropic/langchain/huggingface/transformers or any LLM SDK. A repo-wide grep for openai|anthropic|claude|gpt|llama|qwen|deepseek|gpt-oss|mistral|gemini|llm|langchain|bedrock|vertex|ollama|inference|embedding returned only false positives: Three.js material code in src/games/flappyCurl/three/createEnvironment.ts, "GPU resources" (WebGL cleanup) and "Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" commit trailers inside docs/superpowers/plans/*.md. The app's "movement to game controls" recognition is deterministic math, not a model: src/motion/CurlAngleEstimator.ts is documented "Calibrated wrist gravity to curl angle... Pure" using dot/normalize/EMA/hysteresis from src/motion/curlCalibration.ts; gestures are a simple queue (src/input/GestureInputManager.ts). The watchOS app (watch-app/Sources/MotionStreamer.swift) just samples CoreMotion at 100Hz and streams raw IMU over UDP to the local Electron main-process server (electron/motion/MotionServer.ts, MotionUdpServer.ts).
armo.gpuDetail: No datacenter GPU need. There is no torch/cuda/onnx/tensorflow, no training, fine-tuning, embeddings, or self-hosted model serving, and no model weight files (searched *.gguf/*.onnx/*.pt/*.safetensors/*.mlmodel/*.tflite — none). The watchOS app uses no CoreML/CreateML/Vision/SoundAnalysis (grep returned NONE); motion is processed with plain signal-processing math. The only GPU touchpoints are Three.js WebGL rendering for the 3D games (src/games/**/three/*, ThreeGameWrapper.tsx), which runs locally on the end user's machine via bundled Chromium — client-side graphics, not cloud compute.
armo.evidence: Electron desktop fitness-game MVP (package.json: phaser, three, react, zustand) that maps Apple Watch IMU motion to game controls. Recognition is deterministic signal processing (src/motion/CurlAngleEstimator.ts "Pure" gravity-to-angle math; curlCalibration.ts; GestureInputManager queue), with raw 100Hz CoreMotion streamed over UDP to a local HTTP/UDP server (electron/motion/MotionServer.ts, watch-app/Sources/MotionStreamer.swift). No LLM SDKs, no torch/cuda/ML frameworks, and no model weights exist; the only GPU usage is local Three.js WebGL rendering — so neither Token Factory (no LLM calls) nor AI Cloud (no training/serving/embeddings) applies.

bricklist.llmDetail: Calls LLMs through one gateway src/lib/agent/model.ts (Vercel AI SDK + @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, generateText). Four sites: VLM set-ID from photos (steps/identify.ts vlmObject), market enrich (steps/enrich.ts textObject), listing copy (steps/generate.ts textObject), haggle voicing (haggle/agent.ts generateMessage). Provider already Nebius Token Factory via env.ts defaults (api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/, Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct); no OpenAI/Anthropic deps; mock fallback when key absent.
bricklist.gpuDetail: No GPU in this repo: no torch/cuda/transformers/vllm/onnx, no Python, no requirements.txt/pyproject. Consumes a hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint only (sharp = image resize). The SIA self-improving haggler is harness-only, NO weight updates, deferred/post-MVP, in a separate Python repo, and designed GPU-free per docs/04_architecture/self-improving-haggler.md. Latent AI Cloud angle only: docs mention possibly self-hosting Qwen3-VL on DGX Spark, out of scope.
bricklist.evidence: src/lib/env.ts hardcodes the Nebius Token Factory base URL (api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/) and Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct as defaults, and src/lib/agent/model.ts wraps every LLM/VLM call via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (ai 6.x), so all four inference call sites (identify/enrich/generate/haggle) are pure serverless-inference workloads already swappable across Token Factory open models (Qwen/Llama/DeepSeek/gpt-oss) — hence tfFit 5. No GPU/training stack exists (no torch/cuda/transformers; SIA training is harness-only, no-weight-update, deferred to a separate Python repo per docs/04_architecture/self-improving-haggler.md), so AI Cloud fit is low/latent (aicFit 2).

buildday.llmDetail: Yes, heavily. Anthropic Claude is the primary LLM: app/server.py uses anthropic.Anthropic() with claude-sonnet-4-6 (Ask Stead Q&A) and claude-opus-4-8 (agent tool loop, lines 127-139, 315-393); agent/stead_agent.py runs claude-opus-4-8 with anthropic beta_tool (MODEL line 32, client line 148); the Vapi outbound phone agent uses a Vapi-hosted claude-sonnet-4-6 (agent/tools/phone.py:36). Crucially the red-team boundary analyzer (redteam/redteam.py) already supports a first-class Nebius backend: --backend nebius hits {NEBIUS_BASE}/chat/completions (api.studio.nebius.com/v1) with meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct via httpx (_nebius, lines 107-119; DEFAULT_MODEL line 165). Provider keys in .env.example: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NEBIUS_API_KEY/NEBIUS_TOKEN_FACTORY_APIKEY.
buildday.gpuDetail: Yes — the project's hero feature is a real GPU fine-tune. model/scripts/train_whisper.py is a standard torch + CUDA + HuggingFace Transformers + PEFT (LoRA) Whisper fine-tune loop (imports torch/datasets/transformers/peft; fp16=torch.cuda.is_available() line 164; WhisperForConditionalGeneration + get_peft_model; freeze_encoder + LoRA on q_proj/v_proj). model/finetune_nebius.py provisions a Nebius AI Cloud H100 VM (resources-platform gpu-h100-sxm, preset 1gpu-16vcpu-200gb or 8gpu node, image ubuntu24.04-cuda13.0). README + model/README.md document an actual run on a Nebius H100 80GB: whisper-small LoRA, 1.77M trainable params, loss 2.12 -> 0.53 over 10 epochs, producing adapter_model.safetensors. Stated roadmap: robot-policy training (MARS) on the same GPU and DGX Spark edge inference. agent/tools/ruby_stt.py also does Whisper STT.
buildday.evidence: redteam/redteam.py already runs as a Nebius Token Factory / Studio client (httpx POST to chat/completions with meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct), and the Claude text calls in app/server.py + agent/stead_agent.py are plain system+user message calls that map cleanly onto TF open models — strong TF fit (tfFit 4, not 5 only because TF exposes no ASR endpoint today, which the repo itself documents, and the live Vapi call model must be Vapi-allow-listed). AI Cloud fit is maximal (5): model/scripts/train_whisper.py is a torch/CUDA HF+PEFT Whisper LoRA loop and model/finetune_nebius.py explicitly creates a Nebius H100 VM (gpu-h100-sxm, ubuntu24.04-cuda13.0), with a documented real H100 run (loss 2.12->0.53) plus a roadmap to robot-policy GPU training.

clawed.chat.llmDetail: Two LLM paths, both implemented. (1) Nebius Token Factory is the primary "brain": app/src/backend/services/nebius.service.ts hits https://api.studio.nebius.com/v1/chat/completions (Bearer NEBIUS_API_KEY) with default text model openai/gpt-oss-120b and vision model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct via nebiusChat/nebiusVision/nebiusRawCompletion. (2) app/src/backend/api/llm-proxy.api.ts is an OpenAI-compatible proxy: Claude models (claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4) are converted to the Anthropic Messages API (api.anthropic.com, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) as BYOK/default, while every non-Claude model passes through verbatim to Nebius. app/src/backend/api/vision.api.ts runs glasses camera frames through Nebius vision + Tavily search; app/src/backend/api/judge.api.ts forwards to a live OpenClaw agent. Frontend (DeployModal.tsx/SettingsPage.tsx) also lets users pick anthropic/openai/google/minimax for self-keyed instances.
clawed.chat.gpuDetail: No GPU compute in the project. Zero torch/cuda/transformers/vllm/embeddings/fine-tuning anywhere (grep clean). All inference is outsourced to Nebius's serverless OpenAI-compatible API; the app never serves a model itself. Compute is CPU-only: the backend VM and per-user OpenClaw instances are GCP e2-small (2 vCPU) per deploy/index.ts and app/src/backend/services/instance.pulumi.ts (MACHINE_TYPE='e2-small'), and deploy/NEBIUS.md specifies "smallest CPU preset (2 vCPU / 8GB)". The only GPU strings are marketing copy (Pricing.tsx/Home.tsx) suggesting users could optionally self-host Ollama/LM Studio on their own consumer RTX. There IS a non-GPU AI Cloud angle: they are actively migrating the CPU backend + agent VMs off GCP onto Nebius VMs (deploy/NEBIUS.md, README), which is Nebius IaaS, not training/HPC.
clawed.chat.evidence: nebius.service.ts already routes inference to Nebius Token Factory (base https://api.studio.nebius.com/v1, models openai/gpt-oss-120b + Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct) and llm-proxy.api.ts exposes those open models through an OpenAI-compatible proxy, so Token Factory fit is maximal and already implemented (.env.example sets NEBIUS_API_KEY/NEBIUS_API_BASE/NEBIUS_TEXT_MODEL/NEBIUS_VISION_MODEL). No torch/cuda/embeddings/fine-tuning exist (grep clean) and serving is fully serverless, so GPU-cluster need is essentially nil; AI Cloud relevance is limited to migrating their CPU-only e2-small backend + per-user OpenClaw VMs onto Nebius compute (deploy/NEBIUS.md), which is plain VM IaaS rather than training/HPC.

doberman-core.llmDetail: Doberman makes NO LLM calls. It is a deterministic MCP security proxy that intercepts agent tool calls and returns PASS/AUTH/BLOCK via a rule-based decision engine. pyproject.toml dependencies are only pydantic, mcp, aiosqlite, pyotp, pyyaml, typer — no openai/anthropic/cohere/litellm/langchain SDK. A full grep of src/ for LLM/ML/inference imports and outbound HTTP clients (httpx/requests/aiohttp) returns zero matches; the only urllib usage is urlsplit/parse_qsl for URL parsing in detection rules (engine/rules/destinations.py, secrets.py, tokens.py), and Typer's add_completion=False is a shell-completion flag, not an LLM completion. The 'adaptive learning'/'subjective'/'OOD token' features are pure statistics: learning/baseline.py is SQLite frequency counts with linear novelty decay, and engine/detectors/token_channels.py is deterministic Unicode/homoglyph/zero-width analysis. Notably src/doberman/engine/detectors/token_channels.py explicitly documents that the one feature that would need an LLM (a perplexity/adversarial-suffix scorer) is intentionally NOT shipped ('needs a real language model, which core (local-first, stdlib-only) does not ship') and is left as an optional injectable perplexity_fn hook belonging in a separate package. README states 'no proprietary dependency, ever (CI-enforced)'.
doberman-core.gpuDetail: No GPU need whatsoever. There is no torch/tensorflow/cuda, no numpy/scipy/sklearn/sentence-transformers, no transformers/vllm, no training, fine-tuning, embeddings, or self-hosted model serving anywhere in the repo (verified by grep over all of src/). The project is explicitly 'local-first, stdlib-only' (token_channels.py docstring) and Apache-2.0 'genuinely standalone'. It is a lightweight async Python CLI/proxy (requires-python >=3.11) whose heaviest runtime is an embedded SQLite store (aiosqlite) for audit logs and class-level baseline counts — CPU-only, near-zero compute footprint. Even the optional model-backed perplexity detector is deferred to a hypothetical external plugin and is not part of this codebase.
doberman-core.evidence: pyproject.toml lists only pydantic, mcp, aiosqlite, pyotp, pyyaml, typer — no LLM/ML/GPU dependency, and README advertises 'no proprietary dependency, ever (CI-enforced)'. A grep of src/ finds zero LLM-SDK, transformers/torch/cuda, or outbound-HTTP imports; the decision engine (engine/objective.py, engine/rules/*, engine/detectors/token_channels.py) is fully deterministic and the 'adaptive' layer (learning/baseline.py) is SQLite frequency counting, so there is nothing for Token Factory inference or AI Cloud GPU to serve. The token_channels.py docstring even states the only LLM-shaped feature (a perplexity scorer) is deliberately excluded from core as an optional external plugin, confirming both tfFit and aicFit are minimal (1/1).

enzo.llmDetail: Yes — Nebius-only LLM usage via OpenAI-compatible chat/completions (see evidence).
enzo.gpuDetail: No GPU need. Pure Next.js 16 / React 19 frontend (package.json: next, react, plotly.js, react-plotly.js, recharts, framer-motion, zustand, zod, tailwind/shadcn). enzo.evidence: src/lib/server/nebius-summary-adapter.ts already calls a Nebius OpenAI-compatible chat/completions endpoint (Bearer NEBIUS_API_KEY, configurable NEBIUS_MODEL, json_object response_format) from the production POST /api/operating-evaluation route, making this an existing Nebius Token Factory integration where any open model (Llama/Qwen/DeepSeek/gpt-oss) drops in via NEBIUS_MODEL with no code change (tfFit 5). The repo has no torch/cuda/transformers/embeddings/training/self-hosted-serving deps anywhere in package.json or src — it is a CPU-only Next.js frontend, so there is no GPU-cluster/AI-Cloud workload (aicFit 1).

go-green-ai-operator.evidence: package.json depends on @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.39.0, @ai-sdk/anthropic ^1.2.12 and ai ^4.3.19; app/api/funnel/agent/route.ts runs streamText({model: anthropic(model), tools, maxSteps:8}) and src/vision.ts calls client.messages.create with image content blocks (claude-opus-4-7) for JSON yard assessment — pure serverless hosted-LLM inference (text tool-calling agent + vision), so tfFit=5. No torch/cuda/training/fine-tuning/embeddings/self-hosted serving anywhere and it deploys on Vercel serverless, so needsGPU=false and aicFit=1; the text/agent calls swap cleanly to Token Factory OpenAI-compatible models, with the only caveat that the vision call needs a multimodal open model (Qwen-VL/Llama-Vision class) rather than text-only Llama/DeepSeek.

local-first-multimodal-file-index-via-mc.llmDetail: Calls an LLM, but only a LOCAL llama.cpp `llama-server` sidecar — no third-party provider. Chat: streams from `http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/chat/completions` with model `gemma-4-E2B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` (a Gemma-3-class GGUF), OpenAI-compatible SSE (electron/chatSidecar.ts:35, electron/ipc/registerLlamaStreamIpc.ts:46). Embeddings: local nomic-embed-text-v2-moe via the same sidecar at `/v1/embeddings` (electron/embedSidecar.ts:203). Vision/OCR via @xenova/transformers ONNX models (CLIP, trocr, vit-gpt2, detr-resnet-50) in imageEmbedder.ts/imageCaptioner.ts. README's "Built With" claims Nebius/Composio/Tavily power "heavier embedding and generation workloads," but there is ZERO provider code — grep for nebius/openai/anthropic/composio/tavily across all .ts/.tsx/.js hits only README.md. Only external API is Gmail read-only metadata (electron/gmailIndexer.ts). DESIGN_NOTES.md lists "Cloud embedding / cloud retrieval" as an explicit non-goal.
local-first-multimodal-file-index-via-mc.gpuDetail: No GPU dependency in the shipped product. Inference is CPU llama.cpp with Q4_K_M-quantized GGUFs (8192 ctx, 4 threads, no GPU flags in chatSidecar.ts/embedSidecar.ts) plus @xenova/transformers ONNX runtime on CPU. No torch/cuda/tensorflow/onnxruntime-gpu anywhere (grep returns nothing); no training, fine-tuning, or self-hosted GPU serving. The only GPU-relevant element is the aspirational, unbuilt "GX10-tier (higher-throughput target)" in README — scaled model serving — which could equally be served serverlessly.
local-first-multimodal-file-index-via-mc.evidence: Both the chat client (registerLlamaStreamIpc.ts:46, OpenAI-style `/v1/chat/completions` with a configurable baseUrl) and embeddings (embedSidecar.ts:203, `/v1/embeddings`) already speak OpenAI-compatible APIs against a localhost llama-server running Gemma-3/nomic-embed — so pointing baseUrl at Nebius Token Factory's open models (Llama/Qwen/gpt-oss for chat, an embeddings model) is a near-drop-in swap, exactly matching the README's stated plan to offload "heavier embedding and generation workloads" to Nebius (strong tfFit=4; not 5 because local-first/on-device privacy is the core value prop and cloud is opt-in). AI Cloud fit is low (aicFit=2): no torch/cuda/training/fine-tuning/HPC exists (package.json has only CPU better-sqlite3/sqlite-vec/@xenova/transformers), and the sole GPU-cluster angle is the unbuilt "GX10-tier" model-serving idea.

loopy.evidence: Already a live Nebius Token Factory customer: loopy/config.py:55 defaults nebius_model to meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and .env.example points at api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/, driving 8+ chat.completions calls in loopy/nebius_client.py via openai>=1.40.0 — swapping to Qwen/DeepSeek/gpt-oss is a one-field config change (tfFit 5). GPU/AI-Cloud need is negligible: the sole torch (loopy/memory/model.py) is a ~5K-param CPU-only eviction MLP with a 23KB checkpoint and zero CUDA/training code (aicFit 1).

mmcp-trade-twins-infra.llmDetail: Yes. mmcp-trade-twins/pipelines/nebius_inference.py defines NebiusInferenceClient calling an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API (env NEBUIUS_MODEL_ENDPOINT="/v1/chat/completions", base_url https://api.nebuis.ai), models "nebuis-moe-v1/v2/large". It is invoked for marble content generation, confidence validation, and text+spatial fusion in pipelines/multimodal_pipeline.py. nebius-token-factory-config.yml is a literal Nebius Token Factory ConfigMap with per-trade model routing, rate limits, and cost budgets. SPECTACLES.md and world-labs-integration.md additionally name Gemini (multimodal coaching), NanoBanana 2 (image gen), and Lyria (TTS) as roadmap providers, but none are wired in code (no SDK deps). mmcp-trade-twins-infra.gpuDetail: Mostly offloaded, not self-hosted. The Snap Spectacles AI pipeline (snap-spectacles-ai-agent/packages/ai-pipeline) uses @tensorflow/tfjs + @mediapipe/tasks-vision with delegate:'GPU' and tf.setBackend('webgl') for object/gesture/pose detection (vision-processor.ts) — but this is in-browser WebGL on the client, not server CUDA. Heavy vision (video->3D reconstruction, spatial mapping, temporal tracking) is delegated to the external World Labs API. The product narrative is GPU-shaped (robot-policy export with spatial coordinates in multimodal_endpoints.py, pgvector vector_embedding fields in supabase/client.py and models/marble.py), but the repo has no torch/CUDA, no training/fine-tuning, and no self-hosted model serving.
mmcp-trade-twins-infra.evidence: Direct Token Factory fit: nebius_inference.py uses the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions client (placeholder nebuis-moe-v1) and nebius-token-factory-config.yml is an explicit Token Factory deployment — swapping in TF open models (Llama/Qwen/DeepSeek/gpt-oss) is a config change. AI Cloud fit is low/moderate: GPU-heavy vision is either browser WebGL (@tensorflow/tfjs, @mediapipe/tasks-vision, delegate:'GPU' in vision-processor.ts) or the external World Labs API (world_labs_client.py), with no torch/CUDA, training, or self-hosted serving in-repo; pgvector embeddings and robot-policy export only hint at future GPU needs.

stowaway.llmDetail: Yes. Inference is explicitly via Nebius Token Factory's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, open models only. Two roles per README "Stack" table + ARCHITECTURE.md: (1) a vision model (Qwen3-VL) reads physical POD scan images; (2) GPT-OSS-120B summarizes Tavily vendor risk dossiers. The live POD-vision call lives in stowaway/intake.py read_pod_live() ("Nebius Token Factory, OpenAI-compatible chat.completions with image input (Qwen3-VL or best available VLM)", guarded by NEBIUS_API_KEY) and is currently a NotImplementedError handoff stub; dossier/external-truth wiring is in stowaway/truth.py + stowaway/tavily_live.py. The dependency is `openai>=1.0` in pyproject.toml [live] extra, with NEBIUS_API_KEY in .env.example. By design, no LLM touches the money math (matcher.py is deterministic, tested Python).
stowaway.gpuDetail: No self-managed GPU needed. grep across the repo for torch/cuda/transformers/vllm/training/fine-tune/embeddings returns zero hits; replay mode (make demo/test) is stdlib-only with empty `dependencies = []`. All model compute is offloaded to Nebius Token Factory's serverless inference (Qwen3-VL vision + GPT-OSS-120B) via the OpenAI-compatible API — no self-hosted model serving, no training, no batch embeddings. README notes OpenClaw runtime "deploys to Nebius Serverless in one command," which is CPU-class serverless hosting, not a GPU cluster.
stowaway.evidence: README.md "Stack" table and ARCHITECTURE.md name "Nebius Token Factory" as the inference layer ("All inference, open models only: Qwen3-VL reads POD scans, GPT-OSS-120B summarizes dossiers"); pyproject.toml [live] declares `openai>=1.0` and .env.example declares NEBIUS_API_KEY; stowaway/intake.py read_pod_live() is the OpenAI-compatible Token-Factory vision call (NEBIUS_API_KEY-gated). taskbash.llmDetail: Heavily LLM-driven AI "chief of staff." taskbash.gpuDetail: No GPU compute anywhere. taskbash.evidence: lib/nebius-trace.ts already calls Nebius Token Factory's OpenAI-compatible API (baseURL api.studio.nebius.ai/v1) on meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, wired as a one-env-flag swap (CLASSIFY_PROVIDER=nebius) in lib/classify/functions.ts against Claude Haiku; README markets it as "~1/10 Claude Haiku's cost."
